utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is Case IT-98-34-T, the Prosecutor versus Naletilic and Martinovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, I apologise for getting on my feet first, but I think it might assist counsel and the Chamber, perhaps. I think there was a question yesterday afternoon about, if I understood Mr. Seric correctly -- and if I misunderstood, I apologise -- about a possible issue. The Prosecution does not contend -- has not contended -- that the incident with the wooden rifles that this witness has talked about is the same incident as the 17th of September. There is no issue about that. We don't suggest that it is the same incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: We have never pretended that it was. If that seems to be an issue on cross-examination, we will simply make that known.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Seric.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I want to protest this intervention because this is another way for him to direct the witness how to proceed with his answer in the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think that the Prosecutor is just to make things clear at this moment, because yesterday there was some debate concerning this issue. But you might clear it up during your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is exactly what I am trying to point out. The position that has been also voiced by Mr. Meek is corroborated by the fact that these discussions of the parties in front of the witness are really not justified. And now, with your permission, I would like to continue with the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Seric: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness S, good morning.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday you stated that after having received permission to leave Mostar, you, yourself, filled out the form and left Mostar. We have -- you had two such forms. Did you use both of them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is, after you left Mostar once, you came back?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then when did you use the second permit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: I used it in Zagreb so that I could move about freely in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have to say that it is not clear to me what you are talking about. I asked you a moment ago whether you used both permits to leave Mostar, and you said you did.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but the second one, I used it -- I used it in Zagreb. I received information from some of our people that the police were arresting people, and so I used it there in order to be able to move about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, I have to admit, I don't understand. Let's go back to the first. It is -- the first was good for the period of 8th September to 11th September. Were you in Mostar during that period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then why did you need that permit for these three days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said in my statement, the permits were blank, and one had to fill them out oneself. And when I filled out the first one, there was something that happened that prevented me from leaving.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So unlike the previous answer you've given, that you used both of these permits, you are now telling us that you didn't use both of them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I don't think you understood me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is why I am asking you, so that we can clear things up.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: I filled out the permit and I had a way to leave the city.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you leave Mostar in the period between 8 and 11 September?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During this period of time, before your eventual departure from Mostar, were there any major actions or operations in the boulevard?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were two separate actions, one that I already referred to and the second which I really just observed from the rear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when was the second one; how long before your departure from Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: Immediately before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One, two, five days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was the same day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you see when you observed things?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw an HVO action. The HVO was attacking the AbiH positions, and I specifically was behind the Catholic church. And in that area - I know this well - Baja's unit was also deployed. Of course, I saw exchange of gunfire. I saw some people had been brought from the Heliodrom. Those were faces that I had never seen before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's go back to the action of which you said that it could have been in July, when the prisoners wearing camouflage uniforms and dummy rifles -- when did you learn that these were dummy rifles?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never knew that exactly, but I just concluded because they looked as if they were made of plastic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where exactly were you at that point?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was next to the sandbags in the Liska Street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the last name of any of the prisoners who were wearing those camouflage uniforms at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that one of the men's name was --

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can I please ask the usher to give us again Photograph 15.1, which was temporarily marked D2/6? You can use this copy or the one that had been used previously. Sorry, my mistake. 14.5, not 15.1, and our provisional number was D2/6.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, can we, for the record, have the witness give us again the name which was misspelled in the transcript?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: (redacted).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, can you now tell us where the line of fire was? Can you please place it on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is where the sandbags were on Liska Street, and this is where the front line was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we, for the record, say that the line of fire or the line of separation was along the boulevard?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we, for the record, say that the sandbags were extending from the first left corner of the Health Centre and then perpendicular across the street; in other words, the far end of the building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Now, can you please tell us where you were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was right there at the corner, right next to the building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In other words, across from the Health Centre?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what happened later to the prisoner whose last name is Zujo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you say -- and please don't say the name right away, because if you do, I will ask for a private session. Is there anyone who can corroborate your story regarding this incident or this action in July?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably there is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know a name of at least one person who can?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I don't know the names, but I know nicknames.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Nicknames, all right. Your Honours, I don't know whether we can continue in the open session or we need to go into the private session for this. Perhaps we can go without the private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think we better go into private session just for a few minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Now we are in the open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm just trying to be as fast as possible, so sorry if I jumped ahead.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that the prisoners were kneeling by the sandbags and waited for 45 minutes before the attack, and that the soldiers from Livno literally threw them over them, and then they started running and they got caught in the crossfire. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me what sense did all that make?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't see any sense in it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the action only for the killing of the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that's the sense of nonsense?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not what I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you now point -- the photograph which is on the ELMO, show how did it look. They were thrown over the sandbags, and then they were running. Where did they run, and where did they get caught up in the crossfire? And if I asked too many questions at once, just say.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's fine. This is where they were thrown over the sandbags, and some of them crossed over to this side of the street and started running down there, and then a couple of them crossed over here. And those who were running on this side of the street, when they reached this point, a couple of them fell. They were hit by bullets.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you are -- you still claim that there was crossfire?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was fire coming from both sides.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you saw Vinko Martinovic shooting from the Scorpion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I saw him shooting, but I didn't say that I was sure that it was a Scorpion, but it was a very small rifle which looked like a Scorpion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand. I need to slow down. What was the position of Vinko Martinovic at that point?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was at the extreme left corner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which side of the sandbags?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: The back side, that is, facing the Rondo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far did the sandbags reach -- I mean the height.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean how high they were?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe up to the head.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what was the line of fire of Vinko Martinovic? Where did he aim?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I was not there, but it was in a direction where the prisoners were running.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that the same direction where the opposite side, the enemy side from which they were firing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we then agree that this is your conclusion only that Vinko Martinovic was firing in the direction of the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were referring to a unit from Livno?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened to it? What were they doing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: Many of them were shooting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was fighting, crossfire?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, crossfire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that the same evening, you witnessed a hand grenade being thrown in front of the headquarters of Vinko Martinovic's base. Where exactly were you standing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was standing across from the base, and I was en route home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I recall, you said that you were behind a tree?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's where I took cover after the grenade was thrown.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anybody see you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot answer that. I'm not aware of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can anyone else corroborate your story?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean did anybody see me? Was anybody with me?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Anybody who can confirm that what you said is the way you said [sic] it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know which person was there with Vinko Martinovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said in my statement, I did not see the other person. I did not even see Vinko Martinovic, Stela. I just recognise him by his manner of speech.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have such good hearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. (redacted).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many prisoners were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: About ten.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you give us at least one name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Isn't it a little bit strange? In the morning you took them from the hospital, you were there, they were your people, Muslims, and you don't know anyone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why should I know everyone?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. How come -- can you explain this, if not to the Trial Chamber then at least to me, because I find all these situations strange, and I apologise for this comment, that you saw everything that was going on with Vinko Martinovic, but you were not a member of his unit, you were with the 4th Battalion, and you have been following him as if you were his shadow?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said a moment ago in the private session, I can -- I gave you names of a person who can corroborate this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But it is only you who says certain things. Even the prisoners who were there on that day do not corroborate your story. We have a witness, Witness J, who said something completely different, who was heard here.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm saying what I saw.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Did Vinko Martinovic ever have you arrested after a robbery of a discount store and turned over to the police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us how Vinko Martinovic, called "Vina", looks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Go ahead, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was tall, well-built.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, sometimes he had his hair long and sometimes short?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does he look like Vinko Martinovic? I mean does his face look anything close to Vinko Martinovic who is sitting there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Very briefly, Your Honour. Your Honour, if I can start by -- if I can make an inquiry. I know I'm not dialoguing directly with counsel. But through the Chamber, I wonder, rather than putting the statement in front of the witness and taking the time to do that - we can - but the issue was raised yesterday, I believe, about this witness seeing Tuta at a funeral, and there was a suggestion that that was the first time it was said. And it's in his -- in fact, it is in his witness statement from the 4th of October, 1999, on the top of page 6 of the English version. So if counsel could agree with me on that, we can simply agree that in fact it was mentioned in his statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Yes. May it please the Trial Chamber, Mr. President, Your Honours, I think my learned counsel is a little bit incorrect in what he states to this Tribunal -- this Trial Chamber, excuse me. The issue yesterday was not whether or not this witness had first seen Mr. Naletilic at a funeral. That, of course, is in his report. The issue was that there was never any indication from this witness, through any prior interviews, that he was standing directly behind Mr. Naletilic, nor that he had ever heard Mr. Naletilic speak any words. That was the issue, not that he had seen Mr. Naletilic. That was in the report. So the cross-examination was only as to why he had never mentioned, ever before in all these years, that he had heard Mr. Naletilic speak, and the content of that speech. That was the issue, not the sighting. We've never contested the sighting. We're not saying it's true - don't get me wrong - we're not contesting the fact that he made the statement that he had seen him momentarily in a fleeting manner. But the fact that he had then testified here for the very first time that he heard Mr. Naletilic speak, that was the issue that was raised on cross-examination, not what my learned counsel on the other side indicates. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Is that the answer?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, that assists. I thought there was the suggestion that went broader. I thought the original question, suggestion, went broader than that to the whole sighting of Mr. Tuta. But if that's the clarification, I accept that and I appreciate it, for the record. The only questions, then, I would have for the witness would be -- and, Mr. Usher, please can I have your assistance in putting back on the ELMO 14.5. All right. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Re-examined by Mr. Scott:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, just a couple of questions about this incident where you've told us, both on direct and on cross-examination, about Stela firing in the direction of the prisoners who ran out from the sandbags. Now, can you show us again -- first of all, point out -- I know we've done this several times, but on 14.5, show us once again the location where the sandbags were. And once you point out that, I want you to just keep your pointer on that for a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, can you tell us, from that position, how far would it be -- in what direction and approximately how far would it be to the first AbiH position that you would be aware of, that is, the position of the opposing side?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From that line of sight?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that direction, it was down there; in other words, the only position that could be reached.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, stay with me for a moment. You're looking, pointing -- go back to where the sandbags were, please, and leave your pointer there. From that point, you're looking approximately -- well, I'm not sure of the exact orientation of this photograph, but using the photograph itself, toward the lower left corner of this photograph, your line of sight is a pretty much straight line, constricted by buildings on both sides; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so on that line of sight - please stay with me now - from that line of sight, where would be the first AbiH position that you could see, if any?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please repeat the question one more time? I did not quite get the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Using the line of sight that we just discussed, where approximately would be the first AbiH position you would be able to see from there, if any?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be this area here. You could see this area here, and here there were already the AbiH positions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how many metres, approximately, would it be from the sandbags to that first AbiH position on that line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'd say between 100 and 150 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, all right. If you look at the trucks -- let me just -- if you look toward the intersection, to the right area of the intersection toward the doctor's office or doctor's house where you said your position was, there's a truck parked on the street. If you can move your pointer around, I'll tell you if we can see if we're talking about the same truck. Do you see a truck that is immediately to the right of the doctor's office? Yes, right there. If you can use that for a point of reference estimating how long a vehicle like that would be, I want -- if you can indicate again, if you can, what you think that distance would be to the other side of the intersection, from the sandbags to the opposite side of that intersection.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it can be no more than 150 metres. At least, that's my opinion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this type of firearm that you saw Mr. Martinovic firing, is that considered to be a long-range weapon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, but enough to cross over to the other side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you saw Mr. Martinovic firing that day, was he taking carefully aimed shots down that line of sight, or what was he doing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was bursts of fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the direction of the prisoners. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, we have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This was a leading question, absolutely leading questions, Your Honour. Because a moment ago, the witness said that he cannot say that. So when it was suggested to him by the Prosecutor, he confirmed it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think it is sort of a leading question in this particular situation, but the Trial Chamber will evaluate the weight of this particular point.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, we have no other questions except to tender, as we should have on the conclusion of our direct, that we tender P11.18/1 as the marked version of the photograph used by this witness. We also tender P878.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like to tender our photograph which we have a provisional number for, D2/6, and I withdraw the announced statements which I had turned over to the Registry yesterday because I never used them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Is there any objection concerning the documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Seric. [sic].

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, yesterday, I tendered D1/14, and I said that we need to put it under seal and that I would tender it through my own witnesses. And as far as the Prosecutor exhibits are concerned, we never opposed the maps or photographs as such. But what this witness marked, we have an objection because we contend that he was not in a position where we can -- from which he could see what he has claimed to have seen, and so this cannot be considered authentic. And this is the basis for our objection. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So your objection goes to the document that is the P878, that is, the map drawn by the witness himself?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The map as such, we have no problem with. But I am objecting to the markings because some of the markings on the photographs, I think, and on the map, the Defence of Mladen Naletilic consider this witness as not being in a position to have seen things that he says that he saw because he was in a different unit. And this is all second-, third-, or fourth-hand knowledge. For instance, in Bulevar, if he was behind the buildings in the park, then he absolutely could not have seen what was going on in the Health Centre. And I believe that our objection is absolutely understandable. And we could actually only ascertain this if we were on the ground, all of us, the situation that we see in the photograph. You see, if somebody is in the park, if you look at this park to my left, and he is talking about the events that were in Ilicka Street in Bulevar or behind the Health Centre, then this witness can really not be reliable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. We quite understand your objections on this point; but at this stage, this is a map drawn by the witness, and all the marks was made by himself. And he claimed that he could see or could view such kind of things. So based on this situation, we believe that this document is admissible. We will bear in mind your objections on this very point when we evaluate all this evidence at a later stage. Is that all right?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So those documents, P11.18/1, P878 from the Prosecution, are admitted into evidence, and also the documents D2/6, D1/14 submitted by Defence counsel are admitted into the evidence. The Registrar will give a proper number at a later stage, hopefully within this week. Are there any questions from the Judges, Judge Clark?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Yes, this question I'm directing to Mr. Seric. I understood you, sir, to say that you had documents relating to Witness S's exit visa. Did I misunderstand you, when you were cross-examining him in relation to documents, that you had documents that you were going to show him?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I did not examine him at all with regard to a visa. Perhaps there has been some misunderstanding or something between myself and Mr. Krsnik, my colleague. What I gave to the Registrar was there in case the witness denied something he had said before, and then I intended to use it. However, since he confirmed what he had stated earlier on, there was no need to use this, so I withdrew it. I only had that particular document, and also the photograph that the Prosecution was kind enough to provide to us. I must say that although we are opposing parties, our colleagues from the Prosecution Bench are truly cooperative.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Perhaps I used the wrong word; maybe it was an exit permit. But you've confirmed. You put questions to him, and he confirmed his answers, so you deemed it not necessary to show him the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The documents were shown by the Prosecution, and they were tendered into evidence by them. Oh, they weren't? Oh. I had been convinced that these two documents were tendered by the Prosecution. I do apologise. These permits to leave Mostar. Since the witness confirmed the contents thereof, there was no need for me to tender them, I thought, because we had them and you also had them attached to the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: You're absolutely right, Mr. Seric. What I was afraid was that you were putting certain documents to this witness that would disprove his evidence; and if you were doing that, maybe you would put them to him. But as you said, he confirmed the contents of the documents, so they were of no further relevance in your cross-examination. Thank you. I just wanted to clear that up. Now in relation -- thank you, Mr. Seric. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Witness S, when you are talking about the incident with the prisoners and the sandbags, do you remember that incident? We have just been referring to it yesterday and today. Did the sandbags traverse the whole of the Bulevar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they were only used for protection for the HVO soldiers to be able to cross from one side to the other.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: That's what I mean. Did they go from each side of the road completely so that soldiers would be able to run behind them like a wall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: So is the situation that while the sandbags were in position, a vehicle wouldn't be able to go up and down?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, of course not. Of course, it's only natural that a vehicle couldn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: So what I wanted to ask you is: On that day where the prisoners, as you say, were given what you think were plastic rifles and were pushed across the sandbags into the line of fire, as you described, can I take it that there was no tank being utilised by the HVO that day at the same time as that incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, in that area, I did not see a tank.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you were talking about the period this morning, the period just before you left Mostar. You obtained a permit or two permits to leave the region. You were describing that two incidents had occurred which influenced you in leaving, but you didn't describe the second incident which I understood you to say this morning occurred just before you decided to leave.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure I really understand your question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: You were describing this morning that there were two separate actions before you left Mostar. Are you talking about the actions with the prisoner, followed by the incident with the hand grenade, or was there any other incident that you didn't describe to us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I described all incidents. I just wanted to point out that everything that was happening those days were the things that made me leave, because I couldn't take the psychological pressure against me any longer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Judge Diarra.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DIARRA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, President. Mr. Witness, I'd like to ask you how the late Tihomir Misic behaved, what his behaviour was when the offensive was started. I'd like to know how he behaved in relation to Martinovic, but also in relation to the attacks. How did he behave in relation to Martinovic? How did he behave in relation to the armed attacks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but I really don't understand what the actual question is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DIARRA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I asked you what the attitude was of Tihomir Misic - I think he died - how he behaved in relation to Martinovic at the time of the fighting and how he was, how he behaved, when it comes to the attacks, as such.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: The late Tihomir Misic -- this was at the very beginning of the war, a very short period of time. This was against the Serbs, and Tihomir Misic really treated everybody very well. I can't remember all the details now, but I can say that he was a very good and a very clever man.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DIARRA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. When you understood that your unit was then going to attack Muslims, why did you stay in that unit? Were you afraid of reprisals or were you loyal to your oath, because you yourself were a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exclusively to protect myself and my family. This was purely out of fear. I didn't want to end up in camp. I knew exactly what would happen, and that is why I decided to stay there and to take the first opportunity to leave Mostar. There's just one more thing I wish to add. From the moment when the war between the Croats and the Muslims started, I did not feel any loyalty towards anyone, because the oath I gave emphasised that all the citizens of Bosnia and Herzegovina were to be defended, and that is all the citizens, including Croats, Muslims, Serbs, Jews; everyone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DIARRA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you explain exactly what "balija" means? I know it's a swear word, it really hurts Muslims, but I'd like you to share with us the real meaning of that word, because it often crops up in witness statements.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know how to explain this. At any rate, I know that this is a derogatory term for Muslims. I don't know why. I never really found out the actual meaning of the word itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DIARRA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any questions from both sides out of the Judges' questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, please. Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Actually, I would have some questions that stem from Honourable Judge Clark's questions. They are related to visas and permits. I was the one who was putting these questions, and I sought these clarifications during the cross-examination. I must admit that I omitted to tender these documents. I was quite sure that the Prosecutor would tender this, and that is the shortcoming we have due to the experience from our own jurisdiction that we're used to. Whatever we get from the Prosecution is automatically tendered, it becomes part of the evidence. So we have been dealing with such a lot of documents and it has been so difficult for us to deal with this every day, so now, on behalf of the Defence, although there is no translation into English of these permits that our colleague the Prosecutor gave us - we only have these documents in Croatian - nevertheless I would like to ask the Trial Chamber to allow us to have this translated into English and then subsequently tender it into evidence. Could we get a provisional number now at this stage, please, because these permits show that this witness did not speak the truth, as it were. The commander of all of South-Eastern Herzegovina signed this. It's not an ordinary permit, as the witness said. This is quite extraordinary, and it says that he goes to Zagreb for medical treatment, for medical examination. When we questioned the witness, he said that he was going to Denmark, and that is to say that he cheated in order to get these permits as well. So I would kindly ask the Trial Chamber to allow me to tender these documents into evidence. However, the Defence is going to ask the Danish authorities to find out what this witness put forth to them in terms of the reason why he wanted to stay in Denmark and on which grounds. We have already been addressing them, actually, so these are the additional questions that stemmed from the questions that were put by the Honourable Judge, and I thank you for your attention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, I think this is the time for you to ask some questions to the witness, rather than tendering of the documents - we have to pass this period - which does not mean that those documents are excluded from tendering into the evidence. And if we are still in the process of tendering documents, do you think it would be right for the Prosecution to explain their views on this very issue?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any objections from the Prosecution side?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honours, we don't contest the authenticity of the documents in terms of purporting to be what they are. In fact, the Defence has these documents because we gave them to them as part of disclosure. Let me clarify so there's no confusion. There has been much material provided to the Defence as disclosure which has not been marked as a Prosecution exhibit, and counsel should not assume, please, that just because we've handed something to them in the last 18 months or two years as disclosure, that we've marked it as an exhibit. We didn't make it an exhibit because we didn't question -- frankly, we didn't question the witness's testimony on the point. Now, I think it's improper, however, for this to be handled in this way. If Mr. Krsnik wants to make these points, he should put the documents and put the issue to the witness and give the witness a chance to deal with them. And on those questions -- and in fact we may have redirect on that point. So this is completely, with respect, an improper way to proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: This, in fact, was the exact issue that I was raising. If somebody has a document, and the document doesn't accord with what the witness is saying, that basically one lays the ground and then shows the witness the document. That's exactly what I was asking before, and Mr. President obviously agrees with me. It is very unfair for Defence counsel to make submissions on a document when those questions were not specifically directed to the witness and he was given an opportunity to respond. That's the point that I was trying to make a little earlier. I probably wasn't clear enough. But if you have information with which you disagree, the witness must have an opportunity to explain, or whatever.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] By your leave, Your Honours, I would Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. just like to put two or three questions only to clarify these permits. Although, regrettably, I have already responded to this, actually.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik, you had your time for the cross-examination before. You should have done that before. But as an exception, this Trial Chamber will allow you to pose some questions to this witness concerning those very documents. But next time, just to bear in mind that you have your opportunity to cross-examine any witness concerning any documents. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Further cross-examined by Mr. Krsnik:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, could you please be so kind as to tell me who signed your permit for leaving the town of Mostar and why?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I can answer that question of yours -- I can answer in terms of a question and in terms of an answer. First of all, I got these permits, and they were not filled out at all. I was supposed to fill them out myself. I am the one who typed in my name and surname and also that I was going for medical treatment. Do you really think that I, as a Muslim in the HVO, could actually go and see such a high commander like the one whose name is there, because I wanted to leave Mostar because I felt uncomfortable there? I really don't think I could have done that. And correct me if I am wrong, but that's it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How was this signed, this document? Without having been filled out previously?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was the one who was supposed to fill out the name and surname, the date when I was leaving, and the reason for leaving.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In other words, you forged this permit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the other permit? Did you also get only the form signed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely the same way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you forged it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was the only way for me to get out of town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And my final question: When obtaining a visa to go to Denmark, did you make a truthful statement to the Danish authorities, or did you deceive the Danish authorities in the same way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not deceive anyone in any way. I said what I had done, and I said why I wanted to go to Denmark.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were not put before a dilemma; visa or testimony here?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers please slow down.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Were you ever put before this dilemma; visa in Denmark or testimony in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: I asked for a visa considerably earlier, considerably before I came to testify to The Hague or was supposed to testify in The Hague.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Those are the only questions we have.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The speed is impossible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness did not ask, Your Honour, to see these documents, because he is familiar with them. The Prosecutor actually had these documents handed over to us. So would it be possible for us to have these documents translated, and then we could introduce these documents through another witness, if the Trial Chamber concurs, and, of course, our colleagues from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, it is again, correct. Defence has these documents because the Prosecution gave them to them. However, I still think that, given the nature of the cross-examination just now, the witness should be shown the documents. I think now the witness should have the opportunity to see the documents and comment on them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think that's a legitimate request. Could the usher take the document and show it to the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are these the documents concerned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Could I know the initial response from the Prosecution whether you object to the admission of those documents or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: We don't object, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. And the Registrar will be entrusted to translate it, to have it translated into English, and give a proper number for those documents as well as its translation at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The number for this document is D1/15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Seric, yes. Are you going to ask some questions out of the Judges' questions or are you going to tender another document?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one question, Your Honour, question raised by the Honourable Judge Diarra, and this is a question that stems from that one. Further cross-examined by Mr. Seric:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, are you personally offended if somebody calls you a balija?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why, if you don't know what it means?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I know it's a derogatory term for Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness, for giving the evidence. We wish you good luck in the future. The usher will take you out of the room when he pulls down the blinds. You just remain where you are at this moment. Okay, the Registrar will have a clarification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The Defence brought to my attention that there are two separate documents, so the first one will be D1/15, and the code number on that is 00898517, and the next exhibit is D1/16, and the code number on that is 0089518. I will have it translated and distributed to all parties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, the next witness will be Ralf Rudiger Mrachacz, spelled R-a-l-f, first name; middle name, R-u-d-i-g-e-r; last name, M-r-a-c-h-a-c-z. He is testifying without any protective measures. His testimony will go to background, paragraphs 7 through 9 and 11; superior authority, paragraph 14, 17; general allegations, paragraph 18; count 1, paragraph 25; count 18, paragraph 53; counts 19, 20, and 22, paragraphs 55, 56, and 58.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. As for the schedule of this witness, I think we'll proceed according to our normal schedule.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll have a break during the lunchtime tomorrow. If you want to keep this witness longer, we could have it next week.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: We'll stop at 1.00 tomorrow, if I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, there is one exhibit to be handed out at this time, too. We can do it -- hold on a minute. We can swear the witness first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness. Would you please stand up and make the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. You may sit down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott. You may proceed, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Just a few procedural matters, if I may. Obviously there are some additional steps that are being taken concerning this witness. His native language is German, and therefore some additional procedures, of course, have to be put in place for purposes of translation. And then we have the security that's provided in connection with the witness. The only comment I would make about that - and I certainly don't want to do anything to interfere with security - but I would like to be able to have a clean line of sight to the witness, if possible. Thank you very much. The only other preliminary comment, Your Honours, is that: While it would be clear that this person is in custody, the witness is in custody in a foreign country in a prison, we are not asking -- while we have not asked for protective measures, we are not indicating his whereabouts for security reasons. So I would caution both the witness and others in the courtroom if they could please not ask about his present whereabouts, other than the fact that it will be apparent that he is confined in a prison. Thank you. Examined by Mr. Scott:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Mrachacz. Can you hear okay?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: [No audible response]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, can you tell us, you were --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the witness be advised to speak up or move closer to the microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think the interpreter should use the microphone. GERMAN INTERPRETER: No, no, that means -- there's no point in that, I'm afraid. It will disturb my colleagues in the booth.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: There is a German interpreter in the English booth, and the interpretation into English is going to be coming from the English channel, as regular. The other interpreter is only for the benefit of the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, presumably things will settle in here in a moment. But if you can, maybe move your chair. I would suggest if you could just move your entire chair up a bit so you're sitting closer to the microphones, please. Thank you. Now, Mr. Mrachacz, you are a citizen, or were a citizen, of what some of us might refer to as "East Germany"; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you serve for a period of time in the East German army?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For approximately how long?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: For about three years.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what were your duties? What did your duties involve in the East German army?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: I was with tank troops.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would it be fair to say that you have extensive training in the use of various models of tanks from the former Soviet Bloc, if you will?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Yes, one could say so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the highest rank that you obtained in the East German army?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: That was the highest rank as a noncommissioned officer, "Feldwebel" in German.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps it doesn't translate into an English rank that I'm familiar with, but can you assist us? Is that anything like a sergeant, or can you give us any more help on that?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Yeah, that's the highest officer. "Warrant officer" that would be. That's one before lieutenant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, sir, in terms of your background, did you on several occasions attempt to escape from East Germany, and were you convicted for attempting to escape and imprisoned in that regard?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did that happen approximately twice?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the prison sentence you served in connection with the first conviction for that?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: I was sentenced for attempting to flee the country.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And for how long did you serve a sentence?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Three years and three months.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you receive a second conviction on another -- for again attempting to escape on another occasion?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what sentence did you receive on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: It was two years.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Mrachacz, let me go back for a moment. In terms of -- you told us the number of years in the East German army that you served, but I omitted to ask you: What were those years? If you can tell us, during what period of time were you in the army?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: I was -- you mean as a member of the East German army in East Germany?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: I was trained as a tank driver, as a tank commander, and so I served for three years with the tank troops in the Torgau region.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And I'm sorry if my question wasn't clear. We have the period of time in terms of years, but approximately what date? I mean from what year to what year, if you will?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: That was from 1975 to '78.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, in terms of your present whereabouts - and as we've already discussed, I'm not going to ask you to mention any particular facility or location in any way - but are you currently serving a sentence imposed upon you by the government of Germany in a prison facility in that country, that is, Germany?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is the conduct for which you are serving this sentence -- did that occur in Bosnia-Herzegovina during 1993?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: [No audible response]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: It was an inaudible response. Can the witness please repeat?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Mrachacz, we didn't get that last response. Please.

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I take that -- just so the record is clear, your answer is, yes, that the conviction on which you are presently serving a sentence relates to conduct that occurred in Bosnia-Herzegovina during 1993?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, I want to direct your attention now back to approximately 1992. Did you take steps at that time to join the army of the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Chamber, please, how even the opportunity, if you will, or the possibility of joining the Croatian army came to your attention and then what steps you took to actually join the Croatian army?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: It happened in the following way: I wanted to become a member of the French Legion, but because of bad teeth, I was not accepted there. And I read in the newspaper that voluntary people were to -- could come to the Croatian army. A Hungarian newspaperman had written that in the paper. So in January I went to Croatia, to Zagreb. There, with the help of railway police, I was brought to the Ministry of Defence, and then I came to a barracks which later were taken over by UNPROFOR units. There we were told that an international unit was set up, but there was a long delay for that because new people turn up all the time from all European countries. So eight Germans came together finally, and we decided to join HOS, which was based in Zagreb as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I can stop you there for a moment. You originally went to Zagreb to join the Croatian army, but there was some delay in forming this international battalion or unit. And because of that, you joined the HOS instead; is that what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you find out about HOS, H-O-S?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: A few Germans had joined HOS, and they convinced us things were better with HOS and that we would be able to work with the training of soldiers or people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what duties, then, did you undertake? Upon joining HOS, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: We reported to the HOS centre, to the commander then, Mr. Dzapic, and we immediately were hired.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what functions or tasks did you perform while you were a member of HOS?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: At that time, I'm speaking about three weeks, we were used as bodyguards to protect people there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. During this three-week period, did you travel anywhere, other parts of either Croatia or Bosnia-Herzegovina, outside of Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Yes. During that time, we went to Herzegovina, direction Ljubuski.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us why you went to Ljubuski at that time?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: It was a trip by Mr. Paraga, who had meetings with HOS representatives in Herzegovina, and we were supposed to take over a training camp of HOS.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, did you have any sort of identification cards or papers at that time that identified you as a member of either the Croatian army, or HV, or HOS, or both?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Yes, we used to have such papers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Which ones of the ones I mentioned to you?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: We used to have military identity cards of HOS.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you given any other paperwork, papers, if you will, by the authorities in Zagreb around this time which allowed you to do certain things?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Not at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps a bit later. Can you just tell us, please, if you can.

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Later, yes, when I joined the HV.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And what were these papers and what did they allow you to do?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: We were given the identity card of HV to be placed at Tomislavgrad, and we had a special passport to enter any military barracks or military headquarters. We were entitled to do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In what country -- if you know, what country or state is Tomislavgrad part of?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: I didn't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of what state or country -- in what state or country is Tomislavgrad located? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: It is part and parcel of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you explain to the Chamber how papers given to you by the Republika Croatian Army would give you authority to enter locations in a separate country of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: At that time, we were not in Bosnia-Herzegovina. The unit was called Kralj Tomislav.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you mentioned that you had these papers in connection with being in Tomislavgrad, I believe. Perhaps I'm mistaken.

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: No, that's not correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's go forward, please, and maybe we'll come back to this. How long did you stay in HOS?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Approximately a month and a half.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And why did you end your association with HOS?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: When we were asked to go with Paraga, we experienced that one of us was rejected, and we found out that it was not possible to establish a military unit. So then we were brought back, and then the HOS representation in Split handed us over to a general who was placed in Makarska.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I see the time, but perhaps if I could ask one or two questions on this point, then hopefully we'll be able to move a bit further ahead.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've mentioned several times being in Ljubuski and about a training camp. Now, around this time, were you sent to a potential training site? And if so, just tell us about that.

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: In principle, it was an old school somewhere located in mountain regions, without water, without windows, fairly cold there. It was winter, it was February, March. Training was not possible, and we rejected -- we refused to train. A unit used to be there who carried out their own training, but that's all I would know about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My final question before the recess: When you went to this training camp, because I think perhaps there's some confusion on this point, were you then acting in your capacity as a member of HOS or as a member of the Croatian army?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: We were still HOS at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we could break there, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll resume at 11.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Scott, please continue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Mrachacz, you told us before the recess that you had gone to this training camp in Ljubuski, near Ljubuski, for the purpose -- or what could have been a camp -- a location - forgive me - to set up a training camp. On getting there and looking around, you found that under the conditions that existed at that time, it was not practical to conduct a training camp there; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you do after that?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: We returned to Split. The HOS centre in Split handed us over to General Daidza, and he put us to a unit which was under the command of Ivan Andabak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And for the record, is it correct, sir, that this Daidza's name - not a major point, I don't think, for the case, but to be clear - is spelled D-E-I-T-S-C-H-E-R?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Daidza? Do you mean Daidza or Andabak?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, I'm asking you about Daidza now, please. Did I spell his name correctly? I'm sorry for the confusion now, but --

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: I do not know whether he is spelled like that; I'm not sure. But the pronunciation, at least, was like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, how was it that you then came into contact with this person named "Ivan Andabak"?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Ivan Andabak, he used to be under the command of this General Daidza. And since he was establishing a special unit and he spoke German perfectly and we were a group of Germans, we were more or less allocated to his unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you have any understanding at that time of what kind of a unit this was?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Not at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in terms of time, is this approximately now in May or June 1992?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: That was around about April/May '92.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened next in terms of -- did you meet Mr. Andabak?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Yes, sure, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you -- what did he tell you or what did you learn at that time?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: He told us that this unit was meant to be a subversive unit to act in the rear of what then was the Yugoslav army's areas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just so the record is clear, at this point in time you say "the Yugoslav army". This was called "the JNA", or these were essentially the Serb forces; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: At that time, it was not clear. It was the remnants of the JNA, which mostly were under Serb command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you have any understanding of what army or military group or formation that this special unit of Mr. Andabak was attached to or associated with?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Association was with Zagreb. We were just attached to this unit of General Daidza for reasons of logistics and for being housed somewhere.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. But was General Daidza -- was he an officer in the army of the Republic of Croatia, or what army was he an officer in?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: It was an HV unit, but Daidza himself was a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you consider yourself at that time, then, under these arrangements, to be part of again the HV, the army of the Republic of Croatia, or what unit did you believe yourself to be part of?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: At that time when we were attached to Andabak, we were automatic -- we automatically became HV.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Andabak at that time propose any particular assignments or tasks to you if you were to join his unit or otherwise become associated with his unit?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Nothing was told us, as far as the distribution of tasks was referred to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, did you do something with Andabak or in connection with his unit in the weeks that followed first meeting Mr. Andabak, as you've just told us about?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: We spent weeks -- weekends, mostly in Bosnia-Herzegovina, in the surroundings of Krevan [phoen] Krusevo. It was there that we were supposed to support HVO units and their lines.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what part of Herzegovina this was located in.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I am trying to do this, Mr. President, if we can, without pulling out the maps, although, perhaps, that may ultimately be required.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But can you tell us where in Herzegovina, where this particular location was or these locations where you were relieving or supporting the HVO?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: It was above of Mostar, looking into the direction of the Heliodrom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And for how long did you perform this function?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: It happened very frequently. One could say almost every weekend as long as we were -- for the whole period, as long as we were members of the Croatian units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you entered into the area around Mostar, around this time, did you do anything to change your uniform?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Yes. We removed the patch where "HV" used to be, and we then sew on the HVO patch.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any understanding as to why that was done, why the HV patches or insignia were removed?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: At that time, the UNPROFOR units were active in this area, and not to show that Croat units were there in the area of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then you said this work continued for some time. Can you give us an approximate length of time, for how long you supported the HVO in this way?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: That was approximately until May '92, I would say. Then we had arguments with the units of this General Daidza.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Can you just briefly tell the Chamber what the nature of the dispute or the argument with General Daidza was.

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: It started when the struggles around Mostar became aggravated. Ivan Andabak was ordered to put TNT to a truck with cement, with concrete, and we were based in a little village not far from Vrgovac, and we loaded explosives loaded onto this truck and it was brought into Mostar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened next? And again, I'm asking you this in connection with what leads to your dispute with Daidza.

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Briefly, after this action, we had some combat fighting with -- together with Croat unit and our units, we were to take over the barracks in Capljina. That was a joint action with Daidza and the commander of the HVO unit, who was General Praljak at that time. When conquering these barracks, we had conquered two tanks with enough ammunition and heavy weaponry. After withdrawing from the barracks, the tanks were taken into Vrgovac, and the unit was sent into Holita [phoen], and the tanks somehow disappeared. Obviously, they were sold to some staff -- units -- crisis staffs in the region.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, trying to help the transcript and assist the Chamber, I believe this location the witness is describing is spelled V-R-G-O-R-A-C, with a diacritic on the C.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't know, Witness, if you can confirm that or not, but I think that's accurate. Do you know if that's the correct spelling of that location you've told us about?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. So, after your split with Daidza, if you will, because the Serb tanks -- the captured tanks had been sold in some way, what happened after that?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Ivan Andabak told us that we were supposed to have a campaign in Bosnia-Herzegovina together with Tuta. There was a Raga [phoen] station which we were to conquer, and that happened. There were no more Serbs units on top of these mountains -- but there were no Serb units on top of these units any more. It was an action in vain. But in the press, in the Croat media, it was said that this unit under Tuta had made a great effort, and the name of Daidza was not mentioned at all. And so the separation came about, so that -- which means that this unit of Andabak had separated from Daidza and joined the ranks of Tuta.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you give us -- strike that. Did you meet with Tuta around that time?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: That was when I saw him for the first time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you give us, please, an approximate date for your first meeting with Tuta?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: I suppose that was towards late May 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell us, how was this meeting arranged with Tuta, if you know, and where did the meeting take place?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: The meeting took place directly underneath this radar station where our unit was then based, and Tuta came to this place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who, if you will, briefed you on the action, the proposed action against the radar installation?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: That was Ivan Andabak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in terms of the field operation, you've told us about the action. Who commanded the action?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: The operation, the attack on this radar station, was under the guidance -- under the leadership of Tuta.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After this action you described, what did you do after that? Where did the unit go?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: The unit -- all members of the units went back to Siroki Brijeg.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you understand was located at Siroki Brijeg, or, stated differently, do you know why you went back to that particular location?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Well, normally I issue, because Tuta lived there, and we were accommodated in a hotel there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the name of this hotel?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: It was called "Hotel Siroki Brijeg".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you see Tuta and Andabak together around these days, and did you see them interacting with each other?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Yeah. They were together quite frequently.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you describe to the Chamber, please, what you observed about their behaviour toward each other? Did they seem to have known each other before this?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: That was my impression.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you learn anything, throughout your association with these two men, Tuta and Andabak, about their past dealings or history together?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: No, not a lot. But I think their association was -- dated back to Germany; at least it was mentioned during conversations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
