utterances.text: All right. Well, perhaps it was not very much, or maybe it was. But what do you recall -- what did you hear about their past association?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: I knew from Ivan Andabak that he obviously was in charge of attacks on Serb institutions and -- yeah, on Serb institutions all around Europe, that he was the mastermind behind it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, when you say "attacks", are you talking about physical attacks or political attacks?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Most probably it must have been explosive attacks or something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you have any understanding of whether Tuta had any involvement with that activity?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: I wouldn't know about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In terms of your observation of the two of them together, can you tell the Chamber whether one of them was more deferential to the other?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Well, the command was clearly with Tuta.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you come to understand the area that Tuta's unit operated in at that time?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: At that time, everything happened around the area of Mostar; that is, Siroki Brijeg and Mostar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell us, up until this point in time, approximately how large was Tuta's unit, including those of you who had apparently, as you just told us, just joined him? What was the total number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek. I see you are standing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. I would object to this question. It assumes facts that are not in evidence. The testimony so far has been that the units were Andabak's units, and now the Prosecutor is asking a question, the form of which assumes facts not in evidence. And I also object to the leading nature of this question. I tried to stay still. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'll rephrase it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, Mr. Mrachacz, around this time after you split with General Daidza, did there come a point in time, after the attack on the radar installation, that you joined Tuta's unit?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: I didn't quite understand that. [Re-interpretation] Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And at that time, if you know, then, approximately how many people were in Tuta's unit?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: At that point of time, I guess about 40 to 50 people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And around this time, let me ask you, sir, did you ever -- during the time that you were associated with this unit, did you ever use simply the name "Ralf Rudiger"? And I apologise for the pronunciation, but did you ever use that name without using the last name "Mrachacz"?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: I only was referred to as "Ralf."

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If the witness could be shown - I hope it's been handed out by now - a portion of Exhibit 704. I say it's only a portion, Mr. President, because the full document is quite lengthy and it's already in the binders, but this is only the most relevant excerpt. There should be enough for everybody, without needing to resort to other materials. And if that can be shown to the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, do you have them, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course we did get it in that big bundle, but now I see that all of you got copies. And I know that we all have the same binders, but could we please have an extra copy for the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I thought they were --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, well, Mr. Scott has already promised you to get one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, in terms of Exhibit P704 - and whichever is easiest for you - the first three pages are excerpts in English and the last three pages are in the Serbo-Croatian language. And again I defer to you, whichever is easier for you to refer to. But on the third page of either packet, if I can say it that way, the third page of the English version or the third page of the Serbo-Croatian version, can you look at that document and see if your name appears or some part of your name?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which number on that page is it?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Number 6.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at least by the time of this document, November 1993, or actually the document itself, December 1993, does it accurately reflect that you held the rank of captain at that time?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, at this time, can you tell the Chamber -- we're finished with that exhibit. Did you understand that this particular unit that you had just joined had any association or connection to Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: This unit was in direct links with Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I will tell you, Witness, that we're going to come to that in greater detail in a while, but can you tell the Court now some of the reasons for your saying that? On what basis do you say that this unit was connected -- had direct connection to Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: As the payment and equipment -- since the payment and the equipment were directly under the control of Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, directing your attention to June 1992, as part of this unit, did you become engaged in any other actions around Mostar?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Yes, that was Orlovac and Varda, when these places were occupied.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you involved or did you attend the preparations for this action?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there some sort of a pre-action briefing?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: It was just a briefing by Tuta, and after that the unit moved out. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Chamber, please, the way -- can you describe the way in which Tuta conducted this briefing.

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: He told the commanders of the individual groups what jobs they had to perform. We were under Andabak, and we were supposed to take a heavy machine gun, move to shortly before Mostar, and then fire at Mostar. But since Andabak, because of the insulin injections he had to take and because of his alcohol, this man often lost control. The first action on Mostar was a flop, and so we had to retreat from that region.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: May it please Your Honours, I would ask that you direct the witness to answer the question posed to him and not ramble. The question was a simple question, and then it was answered, and then the witness just keeps talking. And I don't believe that's correct. It's not the Prosecutor's fault, but it is the witness's fault. He needs to listen to the question and answer it, and not then extrapolate from there into another subject. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, for almost all the witnesses, it is the first time to give testimony before this Tribunal. In a word, they are not professional witnesses, and they really don't know how to do their testimony. Most of the witnesses are very eager to give their evidence and to talk about what happened during that time. If the answer of the witness is still within the framework of the question posed by the Prosecutor, we see no reason to stop him at certain points unless the witness is giving a very wild answer. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, Mr. Mrachacz, before, in fact, going forward, and touching on, in part, the answer you just gave, let me stay, if I can, with the briefing for a moment. You said a briefing was given by Tuta. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as a military man, can you tell the Chamber -- can you give an assessment of Tuta's briefing; that is, was it done in a professional military manner? Did he seem to know what he was talking about, military things, or what can you tell us?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: The instructions were very correct, and he wanted to make sure that the losses amongst his own men should be as little as possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. If you can take us forward into the action itself, and you began to do so a moment ago. Did you during this action participate in a group or subunit that was -- excuse me -- that was immediately part of Andabak's unit?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Well, I was directly subordinate to Ivan Andabak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the task of your unit? What was the assignment of your unit for purposes of this action?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: We were supposed to move into the direction of Mostar and fire at the chain of hills.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us how the action was carried out, and was it carried out properly or improperly?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: This action was interrupted because we had to fear that the Serb units might come on us and cut us off from the rest of our units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did someone in particular put you in the wrong location that exposed you to being cut off?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: That was Ivan Andabak, because of his failures, and he also gave the wrong information to Tuta. And because of this information, our location was reported to Tuta as being in the wrong place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, how was your unit -- your subunit commanded by Andabak, how were you in communication with other parts of this formation at this time?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: We communicated with Motorolas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Over the Motorola radios, did you overhear any conversations or exchanges between Tuta and Andabak?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: No, because Andabak was not directly next to us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened after the -- it was determined that your unit was in the wrong location?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: We fled back into our starting position.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you receive any other orders at that time?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: No, not at that time. The only information was "cut this action."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you at some point meet up, as you moved to -- I think you said your original -- your starting positions, did you at some time in these course of events come into contact with Tuta?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Well, we met at the starting position, and there, it was said that nobody should take orders from Andabak because that was a risk and a threat to the people. And Tuta then said himself that we were subordinate to him directly. And that if he was not there, orders would be given out by Lija or Cikota.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall whether there was any exchange between Tuta and Andabak at that time?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: They had talked to each other, and I think that Tuta made his views plain to Andabak. But anyhow; Andabak then only was used for logistic assignments.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, sir, from that date forward, during the rest of your association with the what's called Convicts' Battalion -- we really haven't come to that yet. But during the rest of your association with this unit, did you ever receive or follow an order by Ivan Andabak?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: No, no more orders from Ivan Andabak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, was there a second action along the same lines as the first, if you will, some days later?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Yes. This action, which was interrupted, was repeated approximately one week later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was in command?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: This action was under the direct command of Tuta.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And around this time, were you given command, either some rank or the function of command?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Not at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Chamber, if you know, what was the purpose of this particular series of actions? What was the military objective, if you will?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: The objective was to conquer Mostar, to conquer the whole territory and to push the other troops out of Mostar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the second action, did you have occasion to see Tuta in the field?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: He was directly with us because we were positioned opposite the position of the Serbs that was still from the First World War. We had a calibre .132 with us, and we had a calibre .80 on the gun on -- as well with us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who manned these particular guns?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: The calibre .80 was manned by me and a German colleague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: If it please Your Honours, the Defence of Mladen Naletilic enters an objection. The time frame which this Prosecutor is now questioning this witness is well outside the scope of the indictment and is, therefore, irrelevant. The probative value thereof is greatly outweighed by any prejudicial value, and we object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Scott, could you tell us whether it is relevant to the indictment, and where are you going to lead us?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour, and I will do it in several ways. There is a background leading up to the more directly relevant events, and for purposes of my outline - it's simply a measurement - it's about one page away. It's the Prosecution position that there was a consistent and continuing pattern of this unit and the command of the unit, starting at least in 1992 and continuing at all times relevant to this case, in which the accused Tuta was the commanding officer and commanded this unit in the field and at headquarters, both in 1992, as the witness is telling us, and continuing into 1993. In terms of -- also in the indictment, paragraph 14, in terms of superior authority, the indictment itself makes the allegation that Mladen Naletilic was the commander of the Convicts' Battalion, a special unit founded by him on or about June 1991, in fact well before this time, and continues through the period of the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sorry, Witness. Let me see where we were. You said the calibre .80 was manned by you and a German colleague; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there a particular other name to that type of weapon that perhaps you used or might be commonly used?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Yeah, it was the name "BST".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was manning the other artillery piece that you mentioned a moment ago?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: That was operated by Croats.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in terms of operating these artillery pieces, who did you take orders from?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Well, the orders there were not so direct at that moment, because it was just an exchange of fire from both sides.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said a few moments ago that you were immediately with Tuta during this action; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you do after this action was concluded?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: After we were in a fire exchange with Serb units and our artillery unit failed, Tuta gave the order for infantry to move up the hills.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell us, please, for these purposes, without staying on this item too long, was the action ultimately successful or not?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: The action was successful.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the effect of this successful operation on the unit itself? What happened after that?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: The unit became popular and more people joined it, and more people joined it who formerly used to serve in other units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And around this time, and I believe you've indicated around June 1992, how large did the unit become or what was the number around this time?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: You couldn't say so exactly, because I didn't have the correct survey. A number of people were accommodated in hotels. Other people were privately accommodated. We didn't have the exact numbers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Forgive me. Without asking for an exact number, can you give us an approximation or range of numbers of the men in the unit at that time?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Between 80 and 100.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did other foreigners, that is, I suppose, non-Croats, join the unit around this time?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: There were some foreigners in this unit as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said a moment ago that some were accommodated in hotels and some elsewhere. Where were you accommodated during this time?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: I was usually accommodated in Hotel Park.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, were there some components of this unit that were located or accommodated some place other than Siroki Brijeg?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: That was later. That was people who were accommodated in Mostar at the Heliodrom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Approximately how much later did parts of the Convicts' Battalion become located or accommodated at the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: That was July/August.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of what year?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you continue fighting against the Serbs after the mid-summer of 1992 or did the activity change?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Up to the end of 1992, the usual fighting was against Serb units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the amount or nature of the fighting against the Serbs stay the same or did it change?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: I would say it was approximately the same, because the Serb units, when assessing what their position was, started to withdraw themselves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever hear during this time that part of this withdrawal was related to some political agreement?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: No. No, not at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear that some time later?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Later, rumours said that there had been some agreements between Croat and Serb units and sides.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: May it please Your Honours, the witness is just beginning to speak of rumours, and I object to this witness speaking of rumours. Understanding the rules of evidence with hearsay, but this goes well beyond that. And for this reason, I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Meek. We also notice that the witness stated clearly "the rumour says."

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's all it's offered for at this moment. I think ultimately the Chamber will be in the best position to weigh this evidence, along with other evidence, whether this testimony should be given weight on that point or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Mrachacz, can you tell -- in terms of your personal involvement, the last armed action with the Serbs as part of this unit with Tuta, where did that occur and where?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Where I participated myself? That was 19 -- that was Christmas '93, New Year '94.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I apologise, Mr. Mrachacz. I'm sure it was my question that was at fault. In terms of the conflict with specifically the Serbs on the other side, do you recall the last action fought against the Serbs by your unit?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: That was in late autumn of '92. Perhaps September, October.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In what location?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: The last action was up in the hills.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall a part in the hills, a nearby town or feature that you can assist us with?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: We were based in a town that was located pretty much down in Central Bosnia. I remember Novi Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell us, as we leave this, who commanded that action?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Tuta was the commander of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, moving on to a different part of the questions for you. When did you first hear the name, if you recall, the Kaznjenicka Bojna, or Convicts' Battalion?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: The first time I heard about that was when I was hospitalized, which was in January, February '93.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And prior to that time, what did you know -- what name did you associate with Tuta's unit?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: There was no direct name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how the unit referred to itself, or if you asked a soldier, What unit are you with, what did they say?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: It was just called Tuta Ekipa.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you give us any help on the meaning of that second part, "Ekipa"? Do you know what language that is or what that means?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: It's unit or brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you understand whether this brigade, to use that term for now, did it have subunits?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Yes, there used to be these things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a name for the subunits of this brigade?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: There were two subunits directly subordinate to Tuta: ATG, they were in the Heliodrom; and then the Kaznjenicka Bojna in Siroki Brijeg. These were units which operated in different places.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was the -- was there a subcommander for the component that operated in Siroki Brijeg?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: The troop based at Siroki Brijeg had a commander named Cikota.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you help us with the name of the commander of the subunit that was located at the Heliodrom.

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Lija was in charge of Heliodrom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall a full name for Lija? Was that a nickname?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: I wouldn't know his full correct name. I just know him and refer to him as "Lija."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, around this -- the end of 1992, you took us a moment ago, said you were hospitalized for some time that we will come to. But was there a time, then, that the name "Kaznjenicka Bojna" began to be used?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where that name came from or how it originated?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: I have been [sic] translated it as "convicted units".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And apart from the, perhaps, a literal translation, do you know where the name came from in terms of who decided that would be the name of this, as you've described it this morning, brigade?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: No, I couldn't say that. Wouldn't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you become familiar during your association with this unit, with the Convicts' Battalion, with any other ATGs other than the one in Siroki Brijeg and the one located at the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: I didn't know myself, but we knew that there were -- that there were such units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any role in providing supplies, transporting supplies, to any of the particular ATGs?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall ever going to, for whatever reason, for logistical support or for any other assignment, to an ATG that was located in the city of Mostar?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: For some time, I was based myself in the Heliodrom. That was in '93.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. But apart from the Heliodrom, did you ever have occasion to go to a military unit that was actually in Mostar itself, the city of Mostar? I'm not suggesting that you were assigned to that unit. I'm sorry for my question. Perhaps it's not clear. I'm not saying that you were a member of that unit; but as part of the Kaznjenicka Bojna, did you ever have occasion to go to a military unit in Mostar City?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Chamber, please, was this Kaznjenicka Bojna - I'm going to start simply saying "Convicts' Battalion," if I may - do you know whether that was part of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any question in your mind about its association or that it was, in fact, part of the military formation known overall as the HVO?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: It was quite normal. We had the HVO patch, and underneath was an additional patch saying which Kaznjenicka Bojna part you were belonging to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During this time, did you and other members of this Convicts' Battalion carry any military identification?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: We always had military IDs with us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During this time, in late 1992, early 1993, of what military force or formation did your identification identify you with? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: As member of HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Chamber how you were issued the IDs and, if you recall, who signed the identification?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: They were assigned by Tuta, and they were also given to us by Tuta.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever come to know that the membership records of your unit were also sent and kept at some other location?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: I don't know whether they were kept somewhere. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see a computer printout of the membership of the Convicts' Battalion?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: That came later when everything was done through the computer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know where the computer printout came from?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Well, mostly these things came from Zagreb, all payroll things, because that all happened in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, going to a related matter, did the Convicts' Battalion have vehicles and various pieces of large equipment, if you will, as part of the -- as part of the brigade or battalion?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: We did not have a lot of heavy weaponry. We had Bofors, .40 mm; and heavy machine guns, calibre .50.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I'm talking about vehicles, cars, trucks, means of transport.

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: That was mostly trucks or private jeeps or even passenger cars.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did those vehicles have any particular identification or registration?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: The doors were marked with Kaznjenicka Bojna or ATG.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know what larger military formation this equipment belonged to or was registered to?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: That normally would belong to our units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, did you come to know around this time, in 1993, the scope, the geographic scope, over which the Kaznjenicka Bojna operated?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: I would say approximately up to Grude and in the direction down to Tomislavgrad. Capljina was, rather, our border because Tomislavgrad seems to have been under a different command.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If I can just have a moment, Your Honour. Your Honour, I think it might be worth taking a moment. If the witness could be shown Exhibit P2 and if that could be put on the ELMO. It should be in the first binder. And in fact if it's easier, I can just hand you my copy. Whichever is easiest. P2, yes. I'm going to ask that that be put on the overhead or ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you can see that, either whichever -- I realise in the seating configuration it might be a bit difficult, but I suppose you'll have to look at the screen. With this exhibit in mind, can you say again your understanding of the scope of responsibility -- the area of responsibility associated with the Convicts' Battalion during 1993?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: That was Citluk, Siroki Brijeg, Posusje, Grude. Ljubuski was a place where we did not have an influence. That was under a different influence, and they didn't like us there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You did that rather quickly, but Posusje --

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: That was Citluk, Capljina, Grude, Posusje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how about Siroki Brijeg?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: And Siroki Brijeg.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the relation of Tuta's command authority to Mostar?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Well, it was -- was part and parcel of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who did you consider or did you understand, in your role as an officer in the HVO during 1993, was the principal military commander in the region you just described?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: No doubt that it was Tuta who had the command in this region.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever hear of an HVO commander also in this area called "Lasic"?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: I heard this name, but I didn't have any direct link or contact with these people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, if you know, did the Convicts' Battalion, or the ATGs that were part of it, operate at any time under the command or authority of Lasic?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: I would not know. When there were some attacks or actions, Tuta had access to all units who were involved.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask the question differently. During your association -- during your membership in the Convicts' Battalion, do you recall being commanded by anyone other than Tuta?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: No, by no other person.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you knew Tuta personally, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How would you characterise your relationship during this time? And I'm not speaking just militarily, but in general.

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: It was a good, friendly relationship like amongst comrades. He helped wherever he could.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During your association with Tuta, did he ever state to you his own description of how he felt -- what he felt was his scope of authority or influence?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: He only said that later on he intended to become a politician, and that's it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let me stay with that topic one question longer. I'm speaking now directing your attention geographically. Did he say anything to you about the scope of his influence geographically?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: At any rate, it was in the area of region of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he ever say anything to you or did you otherwise know about any connection he had to the local government or the municipal government in Siroki Brijeg?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: I can barely say anything about his relationships to the authorities, but the absolute focus was Tuta.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Chamber, please - changing topics - at what locations the Convicts' Battalion had a headquarters or a base, if you will?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: The location was Siroki Brijeg, and there it was the Tobacco Factory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And apart from Siroki Brijeg, did you come to know whether either Tuta himself or other components of the Convicts' Battalion had offices or bases at other locations?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Directly in Mostar, in the Ministry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What Ministry?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: It was the Ministry of the HVO units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was located -- in connection with the Convicts' Battalion, who or what was located in the office of the Ministry of Defence in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: In the headquarters, there used to be the offices of all commanders, Praljak, Tuta, so all were represented there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, I would like the witness to be shown, please, on the ELMO what has been marked as Prosecution Exhibit 26.9. It will be in the first binder, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, Mr. Mrachacz, what is this a photograph of?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: That is Siroki Brijeg Tobacco Factory. Yeah, that's up there at Siroki Brijeg.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And during the time of your membership in the Convicts' Battalion, would this have been considered the principal base of the Convicts' Battalion?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Yes. It was the Kaznjenicka Bojna.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And looking at this photograph, please, can you see - and if you can, can you point out to us - the particular building where Tuta's office was located?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let the record reflect the witness is pointing to a square, relatively - in comparison to the buildings around it - smaller what appears to be an approximately two-storey building with a red roof, roughly between two much larger buildings running parallel to each other.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, Witness, I'm going to ask you -- and again it may be difficult with this configuration. Perhaps the interpreter there can assist us, Mr. President, if you will allow. Could one of you, but at your direction, Mr. Mrachacz, not anybody else's but at your direction, put a mark or a circle around the building that you say was where Tuta's office was located?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just for the record purposes, could you also just mark that -- could I ask that you please mark that as "1" or with the number "1" or that it be marked with the number "1"?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, with the Court's permission, I think it would be easier if you mark it where he has drawn the circle, but if it can just be marked Number 1. I know this is a bit unusual, Mr. President, but it's difficult for the witness to reach the ELMO at this point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just so the record is absolutely clear, sir, that is the location -- that is your testimony and your marking, perhaps made on your behalf, of a building that's circled and marked with the number "1"; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Apart from Tuta, did anyone have their offices in that same building, or who else was located in that building?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: There were two offices in this building. One was Tuta's, and the other one was Andabak's, and some more office rooms, and also computers were there and people who operated the computers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, we're finished with that exhibit. You mentioned an office at the Ministry of Defence in Mostar. Do you know approximately when that office began to be used as a base or headquarters for the Convicts' Battalion? Not to the exclusion of the other, but I'm just saying as an additional office, if you will.

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: I've heard that Tuta used to have another office at Grude.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. In addition to Grude, you mentioned a few minutes ago in your testimony an office at the Ministry of Defence. You said that, and I'm only saying what you've already said.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, forgive me just for trying to bring us back to where we were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This was a place where you said both Praljak and Tuta had an office. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know approximately when Tuta had or began to use an office at the Ministry of Defence in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Well, he used it after we had conquered Mostar in principle, so that was mid-'92, July, August '92.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did that continue through 1993 as well?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, again, you've mentioned this before, but in terms of the locations, what we're focussing on at the moment, where were you accommodated as part of the Convicts' Battalion?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: In '92, in the Heliodrom mainly. And then only and exclusively in Siroki.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If I can ask that the witness please be shown or placed on the ELMO Exhibit 26.11.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what that photograph depicts, please.

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: That was the Hotel Park where we were accommodated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Chamber, in fact, what your room number was at the hotel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you see your room in this photograph? I mean not the inside, obviously, but in terms of the hotel, can you see the approximate part of the hotel where your room was located?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: On the first floor, right inside, the one with the balcony.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you've also indicated that you had accommodations at the Heliodrom. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And for how long did you have accommodations at the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Approximately for three to four months.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you the only member of the Convicts' Battalion to be accommodated at the Heliodrom, or can you tell us more about what was based -- who and what was based at the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: A fairly big number of people were accommodated at the Heliodrom, that is, local and foreigners.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you may have mentioned this before, but -- at another point in your testimony, but can you tell us again, if you did, was there a name of the particular component of the Convicts' Battalion that was located at the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: The ATG group under the command of Lija was accommodated at the Heliodrom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Mrachacz, I'm going to ask you some questions now and in a few minutes, what, again, can you say -- can you tell the Chamber, in your own words, describe the military skills and knowledge that was displayed by Tuta.

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: I would not know about exact military skills, but I know that he was a very good planner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he demonstrate a knowledge of military tactics?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your experience and your association as a member of the Convicts' Battalion, who conducted the military briefings for the unit overall? I mean, not the subunits but for the Convicts' Battalion as an overall unit.

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: That was Tuta.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did Tuta's men refer to him? How did you refer to Tuta?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: He was generally approached as "Tuta."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell us, can you tell the Chamber, what sort of attitude or posture did he display toward the enemy at any particular time, whether that was Serbs or whether it was Muslims?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Well, his posture, I couldn't say anything about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, my apology for the question. I certainly didn't mean physical posture, his physical posture, forgive me. Based on his conduct, his words, the way you saw him conduct himself, what was his view toward the enemy?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: It was quite correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Well, he was not biased. Nothing of that sort.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could, just before we break, I would like to finish these one or two questions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Mrachacz, before we stop for the lunch recess, I would like you, please, to look around the courtroom today, and I want you to tell us if you can see, can you identify the person you knew in 1992 and 1993 as Tuta.

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Yes, I know him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For the record purposes, sir, I need to ask you to give us a bit of a physical description, where he is in the courtroom, perhaps how he is dressed.

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: He's seated in the last row, second from the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, may the record please reflect that the witness has identified the accused Tuta.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. I think we'll adjourn --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I was going to say with that, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: -- until 2.30 this afternoon. --- Luncheon recess taken at 1.01 p.m. 21 22 23 24 25

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Mrachacz, the next topic I want to turn your attention to are some procedural matters in terms of procedures or practices that were followed, to your knowledge, by the Convicts' Battalion. Can you please describe to the Chamber any sort of daily meetings or briefings or procedure that you were familiar with during the time that you were a member of the -- actually, more than a member, an officer of the Convicts' Battalion?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Daily procedure was that every day at 9.00, there was a meeting at the Tobacco Factory where -- sort of roll call. And if there were actions, they were then announced to us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who typically ran or, if you will, chaired those meetings?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Either Tuta himself or one of his -- one of his deputies; that's Cikota or Lija.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the typical membership or attendance at these morning meetings? Who would be there on a regular basis, in addition to Tuta himself?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Every now and then, Andabak joined us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who else? If you could just take me -- so far you've told us, Tuta and Andabak sometime. And who else?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Otherwise, Cikota and Lija, they were there all the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you attend these meetings on a regular basis?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you, among the foreigners, if you will, the non-Croats in the Convicts' Battalion, were you the senior officer?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: No. There were a few others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, did any others attend the morning meetings, in addition to yourself?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: There was the man who was in charge of the Bofors. By name, Maximilian Resch.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was there any other non-Croats or foreigners, if you will, who attended the meetings, besides you and Mr. Resch?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: In principal, all were there who were accommodated in the hotel, so all foreigners.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, let me come back to it in this way: Approximately how many people, on average, participated in this morning meeting?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Normally, all should have been there who were part of this unit, because checks were made both in the Tobacco Factory and at Siroki Brijeg, and the same procedure was held down in the Heliodrom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To your knowledge, were there similar morning briefings at the component of the Convicts' Battalion located at the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Yes, there were such meetings as well. They were held on a regular basis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who conducted or chaired those meetings?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: It was Lija in the Heliodrom. And at Siroki Brijeg, it was Lija. And when Tuta was there, then he did it himself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell us, after the morning meeting, was there any Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. other particular pattern or similar behaviour, in terms of the daily schedule, if you will, that happened after the morning meeting?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: It was all the same procedure. When there was an action imminent, it was said, "Everybody will keep close to the town, nobody is leaving town, because we'll soon be out in the field." And if there was no action imminent, then we were free to go downtown or do something else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you observe whether Tuta had a daily routine that he would follow after the morning meeting?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: No, I wouldn't know anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know Tuta, after these meetings, to go anywhere else?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Well, depended where his duties were. Either it was Mostar or some other place. I have no information about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you give the Chamber some idea of how often he would travel to the Ministry of Defence in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: In '92, he used to be there all the time. '93, I would not know how often he was there, but I know that he was there as well in 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did Tuta also travel to Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Yes, he also was in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you give us again -- I will take the same periods of time you just mentioned. In 1992, can you give us an approximate idea of how many times you knew or were aware that Tuta travelled to Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to say how often, but it was several times. I know because when you wanted to talk to him, you would be told that no, he will be back. He's in Zagreb. He will be back either tomorrow or any other day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I will, nonetheless, ask you the same question about 1993. Can you give us any different answer, or perhaps it's the same, about the frequency of his travel to Zagreb in 1993.

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: No, I would say he was more often in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, please, how would it be that orders would come in to the Convicts' Battalion headquarters from any other part of the HVO or what have you, essentially to call the unit into action. Can you just spend a moment describing to the Chamber how that would happen.

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Mostly when Tuta returned from Zagreb or from Split or from other places, then usually two to three days later, one could figure out that an action was imminent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a telephone system at the headquarters that you were familiar with?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Yes, there was a telephone system.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did that operate?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Well, you usually were in touch with Heliodrom. The private telephone numbers of Tuta were available. That means you had communication to all possible sides.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you assist us, please, in terms of the telephone system, were the lines set up in such a way, did you have to dial particular numbers, or was it a system which, if you picked up a particular phone, you would be connected to a particular location?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: In the first time, everything was more or less done through Motorola. And later on, all communication was by telephone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you, in Siroki Brijeg, in frequent telephone communication with the Ministry of Defence in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: No, not me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, I'm sorry, not you. But to your knowledge, the headquarters unit, if you will, the Convicts' Battalion.

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: I suppose they would have been in touch, but I wouldn't know who.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, were you ever in the office, in Tuta's office, when he would be on the telephone with various people?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us this morning that Tuta, and again just now, that Tuta had this connection or relationship with Zagreb. Will you tell us more, please, about what you base that on? What did you see, hear, observe, that causes you to think that, believe that?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: I assume it was because of the fact that he knew the former Minister of Defence of the Republic very well. They were also together as school boys in school; and therefore, this is to be assumed because the Minister of Defence, Gojko Susak, very often used to be in our place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And for the transcript, translation, Mr. President, are you familiar with the name Susak?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Yes, he's the Minister of Defence, the former Minister of Defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see Mr. Susak in Siroki Brijeg?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Yes, I saw him frequently.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Tuta ever introduce you to Mr. Susak?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Yes, he did so once.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us how Mr. Susak would arrive in Siroki Brijeg, how did he travel?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: He made a very good reasonable impression, what his name is. One time, when he came to Siroki, he came down in a helicopter, and then he touched down at the sports ground. On other occasions, he would come by car.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you -- if I direct your attention particularly to 1993, can you give the Chamber any more information on approximately how many times you saw or understood Susak to be in Siroki Brijeg with Tuta.

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: It could have been three times. At any rate, three times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know whether -- well, in comparison to that, can you give the Chamber some idea of: Did Tuta travel to Zagreb more or less frequently than Susak came to Siroki Brijeg?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Yeah, that's true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I'm not sure -- sorry, I don't think that's responsive. My question is: Did Tuta travel to Zagreb more or less frequently than Susak came to Siroki Brijeg?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: He was more often in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your experience as an officer of the Convicts' Battalion, did you ever engage in operations with units or components of the army of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Yes, I remember one such action.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, if you recall, the name of the HV unit that was involved in that action with you?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: That was units of what was referred to as "Tiger Brigades".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what part of Croatia they came from?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: I don't know from what part, but I was told that they were -- it was probably coming from the Zagreb region.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During these morning meetings or in other meetings to prepare for actions, can you tell the Chamber, was it ever said to you that some action was contingent or was being held depending on a decision or communication from Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: No, nobody told me anything about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were you paid?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: I was paid as any other Croatian soldier, the same tariffs, the same salary or wage groups, rates.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I didn't mean to interrupt you. Directing your attention to the earlier period where you said that you became a member of the Convicts' Battalion in approximately June 1992, how were you paid? I mean physically, how would you be paid during that time?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Payment was normal. We started with 60 deutschemarks as our salary, and then it went up. We got lists of paper with our names and the sums on it. We signed it, and then it was transferred.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let me direct your attention again to the early period of time. Were you paid by some sort of -- on paper? By that, I mean what some people might call a "cheque" or a "bank draft," or were you paid in cash, currency?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: First there was an entire list with the names of everybody, of the whole unit on it, and we were paid in cash. That's in Croatian dinar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how would this cash be brought to Siroki Brijeg?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: The money was brought along from Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By who?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Either Tuta brought it along or some of his -- the people around him, because he must have obtained it from the administration there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there anything else about the currency, when you received it, apart from the fact that it was Croatian dinars, that indicated to you that the money had come from Croatia or Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: It was these lists which were printed on computers or were at the head of the sheet, some reference was made that this was coming from Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell us from where the Convicts' Battalion obtained its materiel; weapons, ammunition, military equipment?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: The equipment mostly came from Croatia. I wouldn't know of any other sources. This is just beyond my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were ranks assigned in the Convicts' Battalion?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Tuta established which ranks people had to be assigned to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did there come a time when Zagreb played any role in the assigning of ranks in the Convicts' Battalion?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: At the latest stage, yes, in this unit, because we had more high-ranking officers in the brigades than ordinary soldiers, and this is why a number of these officers were downgraded, as far as their rank is concerned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any paper about that? Did you see a written communication about that at some point?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: There was one letter where it was pointed out to correct the situation, and then this was done.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see the letterhead on the letter?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Yes, I saw the letterhead.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the letterhead?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: "Ministry of Defence, HV."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see a signature on the letter?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: No, I didn't pay attention to that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In August 1992, were you appointed a captain of the Convicts' Battalion?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who named you to that position?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: It was Tuta.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Tuta say anything about your appointment that, again, connected that in some way to Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you become -- sorry. Did you become involved in helping in the recruitment and assignment of foreigners to the Convicts' Battalion?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: I was not entrusted with recruiting people. But when foreigners wanted to come to us, I was entrusted in talking to these people, asking what their qualification was or whether they had any military knowledge. If that was the case, I told Tuta, yes, this is a person who can be taken by us, or I could also tell him, no, we can't take this person.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was it that gave you that assignment or asked you to do that?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Tuta charged me with this task.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how these foreigners would come to have contact with the Convicts' Battalion? How would they learn about the Convicts' Battalion, if you know, or show up in Siroki Brijeg?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: As far as I was told by these people, the officers in Croatia pointed out that foreigners would not be accepted in Croatia any longer, but that they should report to Siroki Brijeg to be taken.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll take you back to this individual, Andabak. What was his role in the Convicts' Battalion during 1993?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: After his first failure of an attack, he had no longer any power of command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did he do?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: I take it that he worked only in administration and logistics. We saw actually very little of him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Tuta ever tell you who you should take orders from?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: As I said, Tuta was my superior; or if not him, then Cikota or Lija. Nobody else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So the record is clear, are you saying that was -- you're just describing that was the state of affairs; or an answer to the question I put to you, is that what Tuta told you?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Correct that that's what Tuta told you. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Yes, that's what he said. And that was the regular procedure; commands were only coming from him, orders were only coming from him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If someone were to suggest to you, Mr. Mrachacz, that Andabak and not Tuta commanded the Convicts' Battalion, how would you respond to that?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: I would say no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you assist the Chamber in this: If one produces a number of documents signed by Andabak, can you explain to the Chamber -- I mean documents from the battalion, orders and communications, can you please assist the Chamber in telling them, if you know, why those would be signed by Andabak and not necessarily Tuta himself?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: It could be that he signed in his capacity as deputy. Otherwise, I would not have any other explanation for that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who, if you will, tended to be in the office if Tuta was in the field?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Who was there then? I couldn't tell you, because I was myself in the field.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, who do you know -- as an officer in this unit, for the better part -- well, more than two years, you must have known, who were the office workers? Who were the people at headquarters that when the rest of you were in the field would do the paperwork, would sign orders, that sort of thing?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: That must have been Andabak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall an occasion when Andabak was given the rank of general?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you present at a ceremony or event where that took place?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Yes, I was present.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there anyone else present there, a notable person who you may have mentioned already?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: As far as I remember, Susak was present, and a number of civilians from the Bosnian Croat government or from Zagreb. At least a few other people were also present.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Apart from being given his new rank, was anything else given to Andabak at that time?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Yeah, they had distributed a pistol, a gun, with a devotion written on it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who presented this pistol to Andabak?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Given what you've told us in the last few minutes about Andabak's role in the Convicts' Battalion, can you please help the Chamber understand, if you can, how was it that he would be promoted to the rank of general?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: I couldn't tell, myself, and I wouldn't know why.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see Tuta exercise military discipline?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Yes, it happened. Yeah, there were two clear-cut orders. I remember very exactly. The first order was related to actions when we were in the vicinity of places. Then the order by Tuta was: Each member of the unit, no matter whether foreign or Croat, who would act criminally against civilians or children, would be punished. And the second was: Five British people who deserted and who went to the other side, to the Muslim side, there was the general order, which was related to foreigners, that the foreigners have the right at any time to leave the unit and to go home. But he who deserted, who went over to the other side, had to be shot dead.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, let's take each of those in turn, please. When did you -- when do you recall first hearing, if it was spoken - or reading, if it was written - an order from Tuta about not acting criminally against civilians?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: That was not a written order; I haven't seen it. He had announced that in front of the whole -- the whole units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear him say that once or more than once?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: It was sufficient to hear it once from him for all people in the unit, because everybody knew what would happen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you see any member of the Convicts' Battalion in fact punished or disciplined for violating that order?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: No, this was not the case. As far as I know, it has also not happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I understand the second part of your answer, but you're telling us, Mr. Mrachacz, that during your entire association with the Convicts' Battalion, you never saw a member disciplined for acting criminally against the civilian population; is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did this same rule, by the way, apply to prisoners of war or was that a different rule?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: With the prisoners of war, if we had any at all, there was only one order, and that related to the death of Cikota. During our second action, we were given the order to make no prisoners.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And we better get a bit more information about that. When you say "second action," the second action where?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: During the first attack at Doljani, I was not present at that time. I had problems with my leg and I was only in charge of the transportation of logistics, of ammunition and food and so on to the camp. So during this first attack, Cikota fell. Then this action was interrupted and the whole unit and the entire unit withdrew.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I'm going to come to that in a few minutes. But then are you saying it was the second action at Doljani where Tuta gave this order?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Yeah, when we were there for the second time at Doljani.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The order again was ...

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: He said very plainly, "No prisoners have to be made."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, going back on military discipline for a moment, did you see any time -- apart from the first rule that you mentioned about the treatment of civilians, did you see any military discipline exercised over a member of the Convicts' Battalion for anything or because his weapon was dirty; for any reason?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Yes, this happened on occasions. It happened that weapons were stolen from other rooms. People were punished and sent to incarceration.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who would impose that punishment?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: The commander in charge of the unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see Tuta impose such punishment?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you believe, sir, that Tuta exercised control over the Convicts' Battalion, in terms of military discipline?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Yes. He was fully in command of the units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I take you now back into the chronology. You said to us this morning that there was an action around Novi Travnik in November 1992. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Were you involved in that?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Not in the immediate action, because this action was interrupted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, tell us about this action, if you know what it was about and how it was that the Convicts' Battalion became involved in it.

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Nothing had been known before it. We were shifted to Novi Travnik, but there was no fighting. We were just told that the struggle -- the fight would go against Serbian units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, when you got there, do you recall whether was the fighting in fact with Serbian units or was the fighting between Croats and Muslims?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: It was said to be actions against Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall whether there were any HV units involved in the action at Novi Travnik?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: I said previously there was no fighting then going on, no action from our side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me delete from my question the word "action." When there was a deployment to the Novi Travnik area, was there also a deployment, at the same time as the Convicts' Battalion, of any HV components?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: I have not seen HV units. What I have seen was only HVO units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You don't recall seeing the 4th Split Brigade there?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: No, that doesn't ring a bell with me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't remember seeing the Tiger Brigade there?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek. You have been silent for about 45 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Yes, I have. May it please Your Honours, I believe that this line of questioning is redundant. It's suggestive and leading.
