And I understand that my colleague from the Prosecutor's office has not received the answer he desires; however, that's the way it is. And I believe it's objectionable, and I do object to this further line of questioning.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'll go on, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, thank you. I think the Prosecutor has the right to make sure the correct answer from the witness. Are you on this line, Mr. Scott?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I wouldn't ask the question if I didn't have some reason to think -- but I'm not going to pursue it any further. I'm not going to go further at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Scott. Forgive me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: That's all right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: I've come straight from trial rooms myself, and I can appreciate the position you're in. I was just inquiring, is there a provision in this Court for declaring a witness hostile? And I don't know if there is, to be quite honest. Is that what you're doing at the moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: There's a number of things, Your Honour, that could be done. I think you're right, under these particular rules, I don't think there is - I'm not sure there is - a hostile witness rule. Certainly, there is also where I come from. There are also ways to refresh the memory of your own witness. But as I said to the President, I won't pursue that now in the interest of time. I think you've heard a fair amount of evidence on this topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: I can see what I suspect is happening, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes. It's a judgement call, Your Honour. And as I say, we'll just move on at this moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Mrachacz, you were wounded in Novi Travnik on the night of 30 November 1992, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened after that?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: I was brought to Split, and I was operated there, in Split.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how long did you remain in Split for your recovery?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Three months.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, if you can just work that out for us. The end of November, so until the end of approximately February, is that what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: On the 28th or 7th of February, I was released from hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were you transported to Split, by the way? Who arranged that?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: By private passenger car.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who arranged that?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Friends, civilians, friends of mine who helped me with that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What other officer was with you at the time you were wounded?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Zdenko and Bim were the names. There was none of them there any more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, who came to your -- first came to your aid? You were wounded. What happened?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: I just sat in the hospital in Split. This Zdenko Marusic and the head of the mortar unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Mrachacz, I don't understand your answer. You said -- and maybe it's the translation; I'm not sure. You just said, I just sat in the hospital in Split, and then you mentioned some names. Rather than try to sort that out, because I'm not sure how to, let me just come back to my question. Please listen to my question. You were wounded. You didn't get to Split by magic. Who came to your aid and how were you transported to Split?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: That was arranged by Tuta, this transfer to Split, and it was at night-time and an ambulance was sent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anyone come to see you when you were in the hospital recovering in Split?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: The persons whose names I already mentioned were there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, you returned to the unit toward the end of February 1993. Did you become involved in an action -- you have already told us about this today several times -- an action at Doljani in April 1993?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Yes. I said in the second action in Doljani, there was an interruption. We had artillery fire. And all of a sudden, the order was stop the fire and withdraw completely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before we get to the second action, let's stay with this first action. You told us before that -- you said a moment ago that Cikota fell. You mean he was killed during the first action?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you driving supplies from Siroki Brijeg to Doljani during the first action?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: We have supplied the unit with food.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was there a headquarters established, if you will, a field headquarters, for the action -- first action in Doljani?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: The people were not accommodated in Doljani, but they were in Bosna Luka, that's a settlement with three or four houses, and there were bungalows where people had been housed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Listen to my question, please; not where soldiers were accommodated. During the actions in Doljani, was a field headquarters set up at a particular location?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: That was down there at Doljani.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was this headquarters? Just describe it for us. What type of place was it, what was there?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: It was a detached house, and there was a fish-growing pond there somewhere around.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the action, did you see Tuta at this headquarters?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was in command of the actions at Doljani?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: It was Tuta.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened after Cikota was killed?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to tell you, because I was not present.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I'm sorry. After he was killed, you said a few minutes ago, I believe, that the action was interrupted and there was a funeral. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell us who attended the -- well, first of all, where was the funeral?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: At Siroki Brijeg.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, please, some of the people who attended this funeral?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: There were thousands of people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. But were there some -- someone might use the word "VIPs" or "notable persons." I hate to just talk in terms of hierarchies or social classes, but were there some notable persons who attended the funeral?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: No, I hadn't seen anybody of that sort because it was so crowded and crammed with people that I just couldn't see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, Mr. President, as was mentioned earlier, on this one I will again ask a moment's leeway. If I can suggest to the witness:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Don't you recall Susak being at the funeral?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: No, I just wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who made a speech at the funeral? Can you tell us that?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Several people spoke at this funeral. It was quite a number of people. You had delegations from all towns, from all locations. And, you see, I couldn't go as far to the front to the rostrum as possible, so I wouldn't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... the funeral?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: I think so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'm going to ask that the witness please be shown on the ELMO Exhibit P40.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Before doing that, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: May it please the Trial Chamber, I can't see line 23, the last question by Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I'm sorry, mike, mike.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: My mike is on. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You have to speak into the mike.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I apologise. My screen shows line 25, the last question asked by Mr. Scott, "Was somebody present," and it does not show who it was and I could not hear that individual's name in my headphones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think Mr. Meek is right. The transcript is a bit garbled.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Maybe you could clear it up with this witness before you show documents, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I apologise; probably my fault.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, let me repeat the question to you. Did Tuta make a speech at Cikota's funeral?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Now, if you could be shown P40. If that could be put on the ELMO, please, Exhibit P40. I don't know about anybody else, but we're not getting anything. We're not getting a broadcast, apparently, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you identify the person who's shown on the photograph that's Exhibit P40?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Yes. That's Cikota.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Could the witness also be shown on the ELMO Exhibit P36.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, directing your attention to the photograph --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Before I do that, perhaps if I can request some translation assistance by the booth. I'm sorry. In the video booth, will you go back to where you can see the -- yes, part of the picture, the text that's involved right under the picture. Yeah, okay, right there, I think. Could I have the assistance of the Serbo-Croatian booth to translate or someone to translate that into English, what is said immediately below the photograph in bold?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The caption?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [As read] "Paying respects. At the funeral of the hero of the Convicts' Battalion, Marija Cikota, next to Tuta were Generals Praljak, Vukojevic and Andabak."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, Mr. Mrachacz, can you point out in this picture -- first of all, do you see Tuta in the picture? Can you point to him, please, just so the record is absolutely clear?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And do you recognise anyone in that photograph that is Andabak?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And do you recognise anyone else in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Praljak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're talking about the tall man with the beard on the far left side of the photograph; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Yeah, this man is Praljak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just so the record is a bit clearer perhaps, when you identified Andabak, he is a man standing approximately the middle of the picture, with dark hair and glasses; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With Tuta being to Andabak's left, with glasses; correct?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: That's correct too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, you said that some days later, you went back -- the unit went back to Doljani for the second action; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was in command?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Tuta was in command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And going back to your testimony some 15 or 20 minutes ago, was it at this second action where Tuta ordered no prisoners?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Yeah, that was prior to the action.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened during this action? Was it successfully concluded or what happened?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sorry, I didn't get the translation.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "The action was not successful. It was aborted."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why was that?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: As far as we were informed, there had been some --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Wait, wait.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: We don't have the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: There's some problem with the translation. Is that okay? Maybe you could ask the question once again.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Mrachacz, you said earlier -- it said: "The action was not successful." And I asked you: "Why was that?" Can you answer that, please?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: I assume there had been consultations between UNPROFOR and Zagreb. The attack had started with the preparation of artillery before the infantry could start, and before that happened, the attack was aborted and we went back to our starting positions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, why have you stated that Zagreb was involved in stopping the attack?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Because it was communicated like that. The UNPROFOR obviously had turned to Zagreb to stop this attack.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you said it was communicated like that. Who communicated that?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't know -- everybody said so, that Zagreb was behind it, and that for this reason the attack had to be aborted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Directing your attention to the 9th of May, 1993, in Mostar, are you aware of any components or parts of the Convicts' Battalion that were involved in an attack in Mostar on the 9th of May?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Yeah, the unit was in Mostar, but I wouldn't know whether this was exactly that particular day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, do you know, was it the entire Convicts' Battalion, or were there particular components that were involved in the attack that day?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: All were involved and participated when we were in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the course of that attack or afterwards, did you hear among your fellow members of the Convicts' Battalion -- well, you talked among yourselves, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: I haven't heard anything from my comrades because I was assigned to the Bofors, and I had no contact with the infantry people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps not that day, sir, but in the days following that, did you talk to other members of the Convicts' Battalion about the action?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: No, there was no conversation about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that the typical situation, that you would engage -- you would be involved in combat operations, and you and your fellow soldiers did not talk about it afterwards?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Yeah. What should you talk about? It's always the same. It keeps repeating. One day is like the other. And we were withdrawing with our Bofors to Siroki Brijeg, because we couldn't use it. And as I said, I wasn't present when the infantry was active, so there is no chance for me to give you any information about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. We'll come back to Mostar in a few minutes. Toward the end of May 1993, was the Convicts' Battalion engaged in an action at Prozor?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you involved in that action?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Yes, I was present.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How was the fact that there would be such an action, how was that announced or communicated?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: May it please the Trial Chamber, Your Honours, I do not believe this is a correct line of questioning as Prozor is not in our indictment. We are not alleged to have committed any violation of any laws in Prozor. And therefore, I believe it's inappropriate. This line of questioning should be ceased, and I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Scott, can you give us a good explanation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, I believe so. Your Honour, both accused, and particularly Mr. Naletilic, is charged in the indictment -- on the face of the indictment with being involved in a campaign of persecution throughout Herzegovina during all of -- at least all of 1993, if not part of 1992 and 1994. It is all part of that. It is all part of the same continuing campaign and directly relevant to the indictment and to issues in the indictment going to, for instance, the accused's superior authority.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Your Honours, paragraph 25 of the indictment charges Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. certain cities and municipalities, such as Jablanica, Sovici, Heliodrom, Mostar, but we do not believe that Prozor has ever been alleged in the indictment, nor is it a part of Herzegovina. It's not fair that the Prosecutor would be able to bring this evidence that we are not prepared to defend against at the last moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, there is nothing "last moment" about it. The indictment has been a matter of record for some years now. It talks about -- and I am looking, for instance, in paragraph 11, it talks about an ethnic cleansing campaign throughout Herzegovina. I agree with Mr. Meek that the word "Prozor" is not used, but it is also relevant to other issues in the case. Apart from whether there were charges on Prozor, there are issues in the case about this accused's command responsibility, the control of the Convicts' Battalion, and this is directly relevant to that -- those issues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Scott, after consultations within this Chamber, we believe that your questioning is out of the scope of the indictment because all the charges in the indictment are concerning the specific incidents. And these incidents we're into now was the date of what happened. And we still believe that it's the fighting against the Serbs or something like this. So would you please skip these kind of questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour. This is, I can tell you, during May 1993, that they weren't fighting against the Serbs. But I'll skip over the incident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me return to Mostar, Mr. Mrachacz, and I will refer to Prozor only as a point in time, without asking any further questions about it. Soon after the engagement at Prozor, did you once again become involved in and around Mostar?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you deployed, you and your -- this weapon called the Bofors, were you deployed in that action or those series of actions?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Not always, because we had only very little ammunition for the Bofors. And that meant that on some occasions, the Bofors was not used. And during such periods, I was involved in transporting supplies and did not participate in the infantry actions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, perhaps you can tell us a bit more about this Bofors, because it does come up in your testimony a fair amount. What kind of a weapon is that?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: The Bofors is a .40 mm gun, fast ammunition.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say fast, can you give me an idea of how many rounds would it fire, say, a minute?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: I wouldn't know how many rounds per minute because it's fired by foot, and the magazine has eight or ten grenades. And they are then constantly fed into the machine, so a lot depends on the person who feeds the machine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell us the effective range of the Bofors?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: The range is approximately 4.000 metres. The precision is 2 to 2.200 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said a few minutes ago that you were deployed on some occasions with this weapon, but sometimes it was not suitable, it wasn't suitable for particular use. Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On whose orders were you deployed with the Bofors?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Whenever the Bofors was used, the orders came from Tuta.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that true for all of the artillery in the Convicts' Battalion?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: We did not have artillery ourselves. Whenever we were in need of artillery, they were ordered to join us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, I apologise. Perhaps I used the word "artillery" unwisely. What other types of heavy weaponry in addition to the Bofors did the Convicts' Battalion have on a regular basis?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Our unit used to have mortars of a calibre of .60 and .80 millimetres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you also have other types of anti-aircraft weapons that were used in a ground combat role?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: No, what we had was a type Browning machine gun, four barrels.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't recall there being .20 millimetre anti-aircraft weapons that were used by the Convicts' Battalion?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: They were there, but they were operated by other people from other subunits, but I wouldn't know which subunits those were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who commanded those heavy weapons when they were used in connection with or subordinated to the Convicts' Battalion?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: I wouldn't know who commanded the other ones. I only know when the Bofors was present, it was mostly commanded by Tuta.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will direct your attention to an incident in Mostar. Do you recall a truck bomb being made and used in Mostar during the summer of 1993?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened -- just tell us about that. How was the truck bomb made, how was it placed? What happened?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: That was in 1992, the incident that I'm referring to, and that was built in 1992 by Andabak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me stop you there for a moment. If it's my confusion, I apologise. I don't want to ask you right now if there was one in 1992. Was there also a separate tanker truck that was used as a bomb in the summer of 1993?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: No, it was a gasoline car -- a gasoline truck filled with gasoline. That was used during that incident.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Forgive me. We're not using the same terminology. Tell us what happened with the tanker truck.

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: I can't give you any details. I was located in the mountains with a Bofors. I just saw, from the mountain range, how the explosion came about, and it looked like a nuclear bomb explosion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall where, approximately -- in what part of Mostar the tanker truck exploded?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: It must have been not far from this gymnasium, at crossroads.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Mrachacz, are you familiar enough with the streets of Mostar, if I showed you a map, can you show us approximately where this tanker truck exploded?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: We were on top of the mountains and you couldn't see a lot there, so I wouldn't be able to tell you about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, do you remember -- are you familiar with a place in Mostar called -- that's referred to commonly as "the Rondo"?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us approximately - and at the moment, I'm just asking you for an approximation - where was the location that the tanker truck exploded in relationship to the Rondo?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Approximately at the same level, but a bit closer to the Neretva River.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, when you say "at the same level," what do you mean?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Well, I would say fairly close to it, 250 metres perhaps. That is very close to this high school there, what is referred to as "gymnasium," and between that Rondo and this gymnasium.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think that's close enough for these purposes, in conjunction with other evidence that the Chamber will have. You talked to the driver of this truck, didn't you, afterwards?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did he tell you who ordered or did you otherwise come to know who ordered the use of this tanker truck bomb?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: No, he didn't tell me.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could he please repeat? I couldn't understand that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The driver who put this truck where it exploded, obviously before it exploded, you spoke to him afterwards, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he tell you on whose orders he had driven the truck to that location and who had planned this operation involving the truck bomb, tanker truck, whichever term you want to use?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: As far as he told me, it was Tuta. And the driver had volunteered to drive this tanker truck there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the time in the summer of 1993 that the unit was engaged around Mostar, do you recall a time when the -- either it was or at least alleged that the Catholic church in Mostar was shelled? I'm not suggesting by the Convicts' Battalion, but the Catholic church in Mostar was shelled sometime in the summer of 1993?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Yes, the Catholic church was shelled with a mortar -- with mortars.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in terms of the Convicts' Battalion, was any action ordered in response to that?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Orders were given to shell mosques on the other side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who gave those orders?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: The order came from Tuta. We had an interpreter, "Zdenko" by name, and what he received on Motorola, he transferred this knowledge to us, all the corrections of ranges and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you recall any particular details about the order from Tuta to shell the mosques; do you remember any words that were used?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: No, I wouldn't remember. The only thing I remember is that we had shelled the wrong building, so we were corrected. And one of Tuta's deputies came up to us and then took over and was then in charge of the Bofors himself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And around this time -- well, do you recall a time of day when the fire was to be opened on the mosque?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: That was around noon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was any explanation or information given to you as to any significance of the shelling starting at 12.00 noon?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: No, I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the shelling in fact start at 12.00 noon?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Shelling started at that time, but I don't know who fired, who shelled, and which calibres were involved.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, the Bofors fired, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: Several Bofors were used, but I don't know where they were positioned and who manned them. This is beyond my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And other types of weapons were used in this shelling that were under the command of the Convicts' Battalion, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: RALF RUDIGER MRACHACZ
utterances.text: We had nothing else. All was distributed and scattered, and who was in charge and who gave the orders for the other troops and parts of the units, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I see the clock, and I can report to the Chamber that we've made, well, what I would consider very substantial progress. Obviously we will not finish today, but I do believe I can finish fairly early tomorrow morning. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. This Trial Chamber was advised by the registrar that this courtroom will be used at 4.30 for another hearing, so be sure to take all the confidential documents and your personal belongings away with you when you leave this courtroom. We'll adjourn until 9.30 tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, excuse me. My client has something, if I can -- my apologies for -- I think we can resolve that tomorrow. My apologies again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't want to take your time. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
